A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Investigating Non-Transitivity in LLM-as-a-Judge. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pairwise-judgment experiments, non-transitivity and position-bias analyses, and tournament-ranking evaluations in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds experiments with GPT-4o-mini and Arena-Hard-Auto in Appendix B.2, Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: Pairwise judging, position switching, soft-label Bradley–Terry ranking, and SWIM Algorithm 1 are retained. The expected-win-rate expression is corrected to agree with the existing logistic formulation; no redesigned method or changed implementation is described.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates judgments on AlpacaEval; v3 additionally uses Arena-Hard-Auto prompts curated from Chatbot Arena. This expands prompt-source coverage within the same instruction-following evaluation task, without adding a substantially different task or domain.

E2.justification: AlpacaEval 2.0 remains the ranking baseline. The hard-BT and rounded-BT alternatives and the six prompting comparison methods are also retained unchanged in Appendices C.3 and D.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce GPT-4o-mini as a judge and evaluate 200 of Arena-Hard-Auto's 500 prompts, selecting model triplets using that dataset's leaderboard. These are settings for new experiments; the original AlpacaEval triplets, tie thresholds, position-switching procedure, and length-control settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 tests whether the relationships between capability gaps, judge strength, and non-transitivity persist across an additional judge and prompt dataset. Existing tie-threshold, position-switching, prompting, and Bradley–Terry-label analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report two judge calls per order, 2,000 model-subsampling trials with 95% confidence intervals in Figure 6, and 50 random-assignment trials with standard deviations in Appendix C.2. The added tables introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 3–4 add PNT/SNTD results for GPT-4o-mini on AlpacaEval and three judges on Arena-Hard-Auto. For example, GPT-4o-mini's AlpacaEval MM results are PNT 3.60 and SNTD 0.1173. Existing ranking correlations, Elo scores, rankings, and ablation values are unchanged; these additions are new-condition results.

T1.justification: Equation (5) corrects the exponent from +(s_AC−s_BC) to −(s_AC−s_BC). Appendix B.4 repairs the corresponding derivation and removes a duplicated erroneous equation from v1 Appendix B.3. Section 3.3 also corrects the insertion comparison count from M−1 to M. These are localized mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about non-transitivity, baseline-sensitive rankings, position switching, round-robin/Bradley–Terry ranking, and SWIM efficiency. The additional experiments support these retained contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains Bradley–Terry's assumption of transitive scalar scores, justifies its use through mild aggregated hard non-transitivity, and acknowledges potentially missed multidimensional capabilities. Appendix B.2 also interprets the added experiments as evidence of generalization across judges and datasets.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-and-data repository link in the conclusion and specifies the new judge snapshot, gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18. Existing prompt templates, model details, heatmap-processing instructions, and SWIM pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Duan et al. (2017) to motivate multidimensional alternatives and Zhou et al. (2024a) to support discussion of judgment biases. The related-work narrative is otherwise stable; numerous other reference edits update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and Appendices A–G remain intact. Changes include localized rewriting of the prompting discussion, insertion of Appendix B.2, added acknowledgements, updated affiliation/publication text, and corrected cross-references. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds two appendix tables using the existing visual style, renumbers retained tables, and relocates some appendix displays as text reflows. The existing eleven figures retain their content and styling; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the paper through targeted generalization checks, correction of the expected-win-rate sign inconsistency, clearer acknowledgement of Bradley–Terry's limitations, and added code/data access information. These improve evidential support and reproducibility. The gains remain limited: the new dataset evaluation uses 200 prompts, and the central tournament-ranking evidence is unchanged.
